10	/**
11	 * Narrow a ranked candidate list to the combos containing one piece.
12	 *
13	 * This is the whole of "pin the item": the generator already builds every valid
14	 * combination and ranks it, so styling around a chosen piece is a filter over
15	 * that work, not a second algorithm. Order is preserved, so the best combo
16	 * containing the piece stays the best.
17	 *
18	 * Returns empty when the piece fits nothing under the current band — the caller
19	 * widens the formality band and tries again rather than treating that as an
20	 * error, the same "a hard filter must never empty a required slot" rule the
21	 * generator already follows.
22	 */
23	export function pinItem<T extends { items: { id: string }[] }>(combos: T[], itemId: string): T[] {
24	  return combos.filter((c) => c.items.some((i) => i.id === itemId));
25	}

27	/**
28	 * The name to fall back to when the model does not supply one.
29	 *
30	 * A look with no name renders a blank headline on both the detail screen and
31	 * the index tabs, so there is always a name — built from the piece the look was
32	 * styled around, which is also the honest description of it.
33	 */
34	export function styledLookName(item: {
35	  name: string | null;
36	  subcategory: string | null;
37	  category: string;
38	}): string {
39	  return `Around the ${item.name ?? item.subcategory ?? item.category}`;
40	}

46	 * shipped with `pinned.slice(0, 20)` and never got it. Ranking CLUSTERS — a
47	 * neutral top harmonises with everything, so the raw top of a pinned list is
48	 * near-identical and the model ends up choosing between twenty variations of
49	 * one idea, then returning the safest.
50	 *
51	 * Same reasoning that produced `lib/generator/diversity.ts` in PR #14/#15,
52	 * applied to the second consumer. `diversify` TIERS rather than filters, so
53	 * nothing is discarded and a closet too small to diversify still yields every
54	 * candidate — the collapse PR #15 fixed on the daily path cannot reappear here.
55	 *
56	 * It only reorders a list `pinItem` already filtered, so every combo still

59	export function shortlistFor<T extends { items: { id: string; category: string }[]; score: number }>(
60	  pinned: T[],
61	  n = 20,

content.text:
I've read every changed file and the `diversify` implementation the new `shortlistFor` wraps.

Analysis:
- **Entry point / auth**: `styleWithItem` already validates `supabase.auth.getUser()`, scopes `items` by `user_id`, and filters combos to ones containing the user's own `itemId`. Nothing about that changed.
- **New sink?** `shortlistFor(pinned)` is `diversify(pinned, 20)` — a pure, O(n) reordering into 3 tiers then a slice. It cannot grow the list beyond the previous cap of 20, cannot add new fields to what `rerank` sees (same `{category, subcategory, colors}` projection downstream), and cannot introduce items the user doesn't own (input is already `pinItem`-filtered on the authenticated user's closet).
- **Data flow to `rerank`**: identical shape and provenance as before; only the ORDER of entries changes, which then influences which single combo the model picks. No new outbound content, no new logging, no new FS/SQL/shell.
- **Sibling-path parity**: the change actually brings this path into parity with the daily-drop path that already calls `diversify`, so this is closing a divergence, not opening one.
- **Resource caps**: still `n = 20`; `diversify` is single-pass with two small `Set`s. No amplification.
- **Test file**: test-only, no runtime impact.

No source→sink path with a missing mitigation exists in this diff.
